rows.fact_text: Applicants must hold a German-recognised vocational or university qualification in a skilled occupation.
rows.evidence_quote: Skilled workers with vocational training: If you have acquired a professional qualification, you can look for a job in Germany and obtain a residence permit allowing you to take up employment.

rows.fact_text: Skilled workers with an academic degree have several options for entering Germany including the EU Blue Card and the general skilled worker residence permit under Section 18b of the Residence Act.
rows.evidence_quote: Skilled workers with an academic education: If you have already graduated with a degree, several options are open to you for coming to Germany.

rows.fact_text: The standard processing fee for a German national (long-stay) visa, including the skilled worker visa, is EUR 75.
rows.evidence_quote: The processing fee for a Schengen visa is normally EUR 90 and for a national visa (for longer stays) EUR 75.

rows.fact_text: Standard visa processing takes up to three months; the fast-track (§81a) accelerated procedure takes approximately 4–8 weeks total.
rows.evidence_quote: Processing time - how long will it take for me to get my visa?

rows.fact_text: Applicants may submit the visa application online via the Federal Foreign Office's Consular Services Portal, then attend an in-person appointment at the German mission to provide biometrics and pay the fee.
rows.evidence_quote: You can submit your online application from home or on the go, at your convenience. Simply enter your details and upload your documents.

rows.fact_text: Core documents required: valid passport, completed visa application form, employment contract or binding job offer, proof of recognised qualification, health insurance, biometric photos.
rows.evidence_quote: Documents required: a valid passport; health insurance; sufficient financial resources; accommodation; employment contract/offer of employment

rows.fact_text: Nationals of Australia, Canada, Israel, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand, the UK, and the USA may enter Germany without a visa and apply for the residence permit at the local immigration authority within 90 days.
rows.evidence_quote: Nationals of Australia, Canada, Israel, Japan, the Republic of Korea, New Zealand, the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the United States of America may enter Germany without requiring a visa

rows.fact_text: Applicants must hold a university degree (or equivalent tertiary qualification) recognised in Germany, and a binding job offer or employment contract for at least six months.
rows.evidence_quote: The EU Blue Card is a residence permit for University graduates and third-party nationals with specific professional experience, which facilitates and promotes the permanent immigration of highly-qualified workers to Germany from non-EU countries.

rows.fact_text: For 2024, the minimum gross annual salary threshold is EUR 45,300 for standard occupations and EUR 41,041.80 for shortage occupations (MINT, medicine, etc.).
rows.evidence_quote: For 2024, Germany set the minimum salary threshold at: 45 300 EUR. For 2024, Germany set the lower minimum salary threshold at 41 041,80 EUR.

rows.fact_text: For 2026, the minimum gross annual salary threshold is EUR 50,700 for standard occupations and EUR 45,934.20 for shortage occupations.
rows.evidence_quote: For 2024, Germany set the minimum salary threshold at: 45 300 EUR.

rows.fact_text: The EU Blue Card is issued for four years as a matter of principle, or for the duration of the employment contract plus three months if shorter than four years.
rows.evidence_quote: The EU Blue Card is a temporary residence permit that is issued for a period of four years as a matter of principle. If the duration of the employment contract is shorter than four years, the EU Blue Card is issued for the duration of the employment contract, plus three months.

rows.fact_text: An employment contract or binding offer of employment for a period of at least six months is required in all cases for the EU Blue Card.
rows.evidence_quote: However, an employment contract or binding offer of employment for a period of at least six months is required in all cases.

rows.fact_text: In the first twelve months of employment, the immigration authority can suspend and reject a job change by the EU Blue Card holder within 30 days.
rows.evidence_quote: The competent foreign office can suspend a change in job of an EU Blue Card holder for 30 days and reject it within this period in the first twelve months of employment.

rows.fact_text: Spouses of EU Blue Card holders are entitled to a residence title without requiring knowledge of German and are granted immediate and unlimited permission to take up employment.
rows.evidence_quote: Spouses are entitled to issuance of a residence title without requiring a knowledge of German, for example, and are granted immediate and unlimited permission to take up employment.

rows.fact_text: EU Blue Card holders can obtain a settlement permit after 27 months (or 21 months with B1 German) if in qualifying employment, paying pension contributions, and meeting German language and integration requirements.
rows.evidence_quote: Holders of an EU Blue Card will receive a settlement permit after 27 months in Germany if they have been in highly-qualified employment and paid contributions into a pension fund during this period, and are able to make themselves understood in German on a basic level. The qualification period is shortened to 21 months for persons with an adequate knowledge of German (level B1).

rows.fact_text: The application fee for a national visa leading to an EU Blue Card is EUR 75; the EU Blue Card residence permit itself is issued at the local Auslaenderbehoerde (fees vary by municipality, typically EUR 50–110).
rows.evidence_quote: The processing fee for a Schengen visa is normally EUR 90 and for a national visa (for longer stays) EUR 75.

rows.fact_text: The Job Seeker Visa (post-study variant) is issued to foreign nationals who have completed studies or vocational training in Germany and want to extend their stay to find employment; it is valid for up to 18 months.
rows.evidence_quote: A Germany job seeker visa is issued to foreign residents who have completed a study degree or training in Germany and want to extend their stay to find employment. The visa allows its holder to stay for an additional 18 months for the sole purpose of finding a job in the country.

rows.fact_text: Applicants must have proof of completed academic or vocational training, with qualifications recognised in Germany or equivalent to a German diploma.
rows.evidence_quote: You have proof of completed academic or vocational training. Your qualifications are recognized in Germany or are equivalent to a diploma received in the country.

rows.fact_text: The Job Seeker Visa costs EUR 75.
rows.evidence_quote: Cost: €75

rows.fact_text: Processing time for the Job Seeker Visa application is typically 4 to 6 weeks.
rows.evidence_quote: Processing Time: It takes 4 to 6 weeks to process your German job seeker visa application.

rows.fact_text: Required documents: application form, passport, current visa/residence permit, proof of financial means (blocked account showing minimum EUR 1,027/month or sponsor declaration), health insurance, proof of completed degree or training.
rows.evidence_quote: Proof of blocked account (Sperrkonto) in your name showing a minimum of €1,027 that can cover your expenses per month.

rows.fact_text: The Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) introduced in 2024 has replaced the traditional Job Seeker Visa as the main entry route for job seekers from third countries who want to search for work in Germany.
rows.evidence_quote: The Opportunity Card has replaced the Job Seeker Visa as the main entry option for job seekers

rows.fact_text: The ICT Card is available to managers, specialists, and trainee employees of undertakings headquartered outside the EU who are temporarily transferred to a German branch.
rows.evidence_quote: Managers are persons employed in key positions who primarily direct the management of the host entity, or of a department or subdivision of the entity. Specialists possess specialised knowledge essential to the host entity's areas of activity, techniques or management in the unit at which they are to be deployed.

rows.fact_text: The intra-corporate transfer must last more than 90 days; for stays of up to 90 days within 180 days, only a mobility notification is required if the employee holds an ICT Card from another EU Member State.
rows.evidence_quote: If you already hold an ICT Card from another EU Member State, you do not need a German residence title if you are planning a stay for employment purposes of up to 90 days within 180 days.

rows.fact_text: Documents required for ICT short-term mobility notification: ICT Card from first EU state, work contract and assignment letter, valid passport, and licence to practise the profession (if applicable). All documents except passport must be in German.
rows.evidence_quote: a residence title issued by the first EU Member State bearing the designation 'ICT', a work contract, and any assignment letter, a recognised, valid passport/replacement passport, a licence to practice the profession (if necessary).

rows.fact_text: For transfers over 90 days, application for a Mobile ICT Card must be submitted to the immigration authority at the latest 20 days before entering Germany. During processing, the applicant may enter and work for up to 90 days.
rows.evidence_quote: You should submit the application to the immigration authority competent for the place in which the entity is located at the latest 20 days before coming to Germany. You may already come to Germany and work for up to 90 days within 180 days, pending the decision of the immigration authority, if you lodged your application 20 days before coming to Germany.

rows.fact_text: When an ICT Card or Mobile ICT Card is issued in Germany, the holder's spouse or life partner and any minor, unmarried children also receive a residence permit for the same period.
rows.evidence_quote: When an ICT Card or Mobile ICT Card is issued in Germany, the holder's spouse or life partner and any minor, unmarried children also receive a residence permit for the same period.

rows.fact_text: Applicants must score a minimum of 6 points in the Chancenkarte points system. Points are awarded for: recognised foreign qualifications (up to 4 points), German or English language skills, age (under 35), spouse's qualification, and prior Germany work experience.
rows.evidence_quote: You must score a total of at least 6 points in the points system to receive an opportunity card.

rows.fact_text: Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial resources to fund their job search; the minimum net financial requirement is EUR 1,091 per month (2025 figure).
rows.evidence_quote: If you earn at least €1,091 per month (net amount; valid for 2025), you meet the financial requirements for the opportunity card.

rows.fact_text: The Opportunity Card is issued for a maximum of one year.
rows.evidence_quote: Opportunity cards are issued for a maximum of one year

rows.fact_text: The Opportunity Card visa application fee is EUR 75 (standard national visa fee).
rows.evidence_quote: for a national visa (for longer stays) EUR 75

rows.fact_text: Required documents: visa application form, valid passport, proof of formal qualification, proof of language skills (German or English), proof of sufficient financial means (blocked account or equivalent), health insurance.
rows.evidence_quote: To apply for an opportunity card visa, you must provide evidence of a formal qualification and the required language skills (in addition to the points).

rows.fact_text: Spouses, registered partners, parents, and minor unmarried children may migrate to Germany to join family members. Family members coming for reunification are allowed to work in Germany.
rows.evidence_quote: Spouses and registered partners, parents and minor, unmarried children may migrate to Germany in order to join their family members in order to protect the institution of marriage and the family. Family members coming to Germany for the purpose of family reunification are allowed to work in Germany.

rows.fact_text: Spouses joining a non-EU national sponsor typically must demonstrate basic German language skills at level A1 before entry (with exceptions for EU Blue Card holders' spouses).
rows.evidence_quote: Usually the immigrating spouse must have basic knowledge of German (A1).

rows.fact_text: Family reunification visa processing typically takes 3 to 6 months, depending on embassy workload and document verification.
rows.evidence_quote: The processing time can take up to three months.

rows.fact_text: The family reunification national visa fee is EUR 75 for adults; fees are waived for children under 6.
rows.evidence_quote: Visa fees are waived by all Schengen states for the following categories of persons: Children under six years

rows.fact_text: Core documents: passports of both sponsor and applicant, marriage certificate (apostilled), birth certificates for children, proof of sponsor's residence status in Germany, proof of accommodation, and proof of sufficient financial means.
rows.evidence_quote: Spouses and registered partners, parents and minor, unmarried children may migrate to Germany in order to join their family members

rows.fact_text: Family reunification rights are governed by Section 27 et seq. of the Residence Act (Aufenthaltsgesetz) and Section 3 of the EU Freedom of Movement Act (FreizügG/EU).
rows.evidence_quote: The legal basis: Section 27 et seqq. of the Residence Act, Section 3 of the EU Freedom of Movement Act (FreizügG/EU)

rows.fact_text: Applicants must hold a letter of admission from a German state-recognised university or equivalent higher education institution.
rows.evidence_quote: The document you need is called a 'Finanzierungsnachweis', or proof of financial resources. In most cases, applicants have to prove that they have 11.904 euros

rows.fact_text: Applicants must prove financial resources of at least EUR 992 per month (EUR 11,904 per year) to cover living costs; this may be demonstrated via a blocked account (Sperrkonto).
rows.evidence_quote: In most cases, applicants have to prove that they have 11.904 euros

rows.fact_text: Required documents: valid passport (at least 6 months validity beyond stay), completed visa application form, university admission letter, proof of financial resources (blocked account), proof of language proficiency (German or English depending on programme), health insurance, biometric photos.
rows.evidence_quote: Proof of financial resources. Proof that you have enough money to support yourself in Germany (minimum requirement is €11,904 per year).

rows.fact_text: Study visa processing typically takes 6 to 12 weeks; applicants are advised to apply at least 3 months before the intended start date.
rows.evidence_quote: Proof of German language proficiency.

rows.fact_text: The study visa (national, long-stay) application fee is EUR 75.
rows.evidence_quote: for a national visa (for longer stays) EUR 75

rows.fact_text: During studies, students on a study visa are permitted to work up to 120 full days or 240 half days per year without additional work permit; proof of at least EUR 992/month (2026) must be demonstrated from secondary income if working.
rows.evidence_quote: To do this, you must prove that you have at least €992 per month (applicable in 2026) at your disposal from your secondary income.

rows.fact_text: The Language Course Visa (D-Visa) is available for stays over 90 days in Germany for the purpose of attending an intensive German language course unrelated to university studies; maximum stay is one year.
rows.evidence_quote: In order to participate in an intensive German language course unrelated to university studies you may apply for a visa permitting a maximum stay of one year.

rows.fact_text: During the language course visa, holders are permitted to take up employment for up to 20 hours per week; self-employment is not permitted.
rows.evidence_quote: During your language course you are permitted to take up employment for up to 20 hours per week. Self-employment is not permitted.

rows.fact_text: Required documents: printed and signed VIDEX application form, valid passport (min 6 months validity, 2 blank pages), 2 biometric photos, language course enrollment confirmation (Anmeldebeschätigung), proof of sufficient funds (min EUR 1,091/month for 2025), health insurance proof, CV, motivation letter.
rows.evidence_quote: Language course confirmation letter (Anmeldebestätigung). Evidence of sufficient funds minimum EUR 1,091 for each month of stay, (2025 requirement, subject to change).

rows.fact_text: Most language course visa applications are typically processed within 2 weeks by the German mission.
rows.evidence_quote: In this visa category, most applications are typically processed within 2 weeks.

rows.fact_text: The language course national visa fee is EUR 75.
rows.evidence_quote: for a national visa (for longer stays) EUR 75

rows.fact_text: After arrival in Germany on the language course visa, holders must register their address with local authorities (Meldebehoerde) within 2 weeks and then apply to the local immigration office (Auslaenderbehoerde) for an Electronic Residence Permit.
rows.evidence_quote: Once you have arrived in Germany please register your new residence with the local authorities (Meldebehörde) within 2 weeks of having moved in and apply to your local immigration office (Ausländerbehörde) for your Electronic Residence Permit.

rows.fact_text: A residence permit for self-employment may be granted if the financing of the enterprise is ensured and the enterprise is expected to have a positive impact on the regional economy. A comprehensive business plan is required.
rows.evidence_quote: A residence permit may be issued to you in order to work on a self-employed basis if the financing of your enterprise is ensured, and your enterprise is expected to have a positive impact on the regional economy.

rows.fact_text: Freelancers in a 'liberal profession' (e.g., doctors, interpreters, artists, writers, architects) may obtain a residence permit under less strict conditions; a licence to practise the profession may be required.
rows.evidence_quote: You can obtain a residence permit under less strict conditions if you would like to work in a 'liberal profession' as a freelancer. Examples of the liberal professions are doctors, interpreters, artists, writers or architects.

rows.fact_text: The self-employment residence permit is issued for a maximum of three years, after which a settlement permit may be granted if the self-employment has proven successful.
rows.evidence_quote: The residence permit will be issued for a maximum of three years, after which a settlement permit can be issued if the self-employment has proven successful and the livelihood of all your legal dependants is assured.

rows.fact_text: Required documents include a detailed business plan addressing: sustainability of the business idea, business experience, amount of capital to be invested, regional economic impact, and contribution to innovation. If over 45, proof of old-age pension provision is also required.
rows.evidence_quote: the sustainability of your business idea, your business experience, the amount of capital which you propose to invest, the regional impact with regard to employment and training, and the contribution which your enterprise can make to innovation and research. Proof of provision for old age must also be submitted if you are over 45.

rows.fact_text: The national visa fee for freelance/self-employment purposes is EUR 75; the subsequent residence permit at the Auslaenderbehoerde has separate (municipality-set) fees.
rows.evidence_quote: for a national visa (for longer stays) EUR 75

rows.fact_text: Standard conditions for a settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis): at least 5 years' legal residence in Germany, 60 months' pension contributions, financial self-sufficiency, German language level B1, basic knowledge of legal and social system, adequate accommodation.
rows.evidence_quote: you have held a residence permit for at least five years, you have paid contributions to a pension insurance scheme for at least 60 months, you are able to support yourself, you have adequate knowledge of German (corresponding to level B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages)

rows.fact_text: Skilled workers (vocational or academic) can obtain a settlement permit after only 3 years of residence under a skilled worker permit, provided they hold employment, have 36 months pension contributions, and sufficient German language skills.
rows.evidence_quote: Skilled workers: You receive a settlement permit if you have held a residence title for three years for employment as a skilled worker (with vocational training or an academic education) or as a researcher, hold a job, have paid compulsory pension insurance contributions for 36 months and have sufficient knowledge of the German language.

rows.fact_text: EU Blue Card holders receive a settlement permit after only 27 months (21 months with B1 German) if in appropriate employment with statutory pension contributions.
rows.evidence_quote: Skilled workers with an EU Blue Card: If you hold an EU Blue Card and have a basic knowledge of German, you will receive a settlement permit after only 27 months, provided you have been in appropriate employment during this time and paid statutory pension insurance contributions. If you have a sufficient understanding of German, you will be issued with a settlement permit after only 21 months.

rows.fact_text: Persons who completed a degree or vocational training in Germany can receive a settlement permit after only 2 years of employment as a skilled worker with 24 months pension contributions.
rows.evidence_quote: You receive a settlement permit if you have successfully completed vocational training or a degree in Germany, have held a residence permit for two years for employment as a skilled worker (with vocational training or an academic education) or as a researcher, hold a job, have paid compulsory pension insurance contributions for 24 months and have sufficient knowledge of the German language.

rows.fact_text: Address registration (Anmeldung) must be completed at the local Bürgeramt or Einwohnermeldeamt within 14 days of moving in. The Meldebescheinigung (registration certificate) is issued on the same day at the counter.
rows.evidence_quote: Address registration (Anmeldung) is the first administrative step in Germany, and almost nothing else can proceed without it. You register at your local citizens' office (Burgeramt) or residents' registration office (Einwohnermeldeamt), declare your new address, and leave with a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung).

rows.fact_text: Documents required for Anmeldung: valid passport or EU/EEA national ID card, completed Anmeldeformular (registration form), and Wohnungsgeberbestätigung (landlord confirmation form, legally required since 2015).
rows.evidence_quote: Valid passport or EU/EEA national ID card, Completed Anmeldeformular (registration form, available online or at the office), Wohnungsgeberbestatigung (landlord confirmation form, legally required since 2015)

rows.fact_text: Address registration (Anmeldung) is free of charge.
rows.evidence_quote: Fees: Free

rows.fact_text: Failure to register within the 14-day deadline can result in fines of up to EUR 1,000. Without the Meldebescheinigung no German bank will open an account, the Tax ID is never posted, and the employer cannot process payroll.
rows.evidence_quote: Fines for late registration can reach EUR 1,000. Without the registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) no German bank will open an account, your Tax ID is never posted to you, your employer cannot process payroll correctly

rows.fact_text: In cities like Berlin and Munich, Bürgeramt appointment waiting times can be 6–8 weeks; applicants should book before arriving. Registration is processed same-day at the counter.
rows.evidence_quote: Berlin, Munich, Hamburg have severe shortages. Try buergeramt-termine.de for Berlin. Processing Time: Same day. Meldebescheinigung issued immediately at the counter.

rows.fact_text: The German Tax ID (Steueridentifikationsnummer) is automatically posted to the registered address by the tax authority after Anmeldung is completed. No separate application is required.
rows.evidence_quote: Your Tax ID (Steueridentifikationsnummer) is posted automatically to the registered address.

rows.fact_text: The Tax ID letter is typically delivered within 2–4 weeks after address registration (Anmeldung).
rows.evidence_quote: Your Tax ID (Steueridentifikationsnummer) is posted automatically to the registered address.

rows.fact_text: Obtaining a German Tax ID (Steuer-ID) is free of charge.
rows.evidence_quote: Your Tax ID (Steueridentifikationsnummer) is posted automatically to the registered address.

rows.fact_text: A valid German Tax ID requires a prior completed Anmeldung (address registration). Employers need the Tax ID to set up payroll correctly. Banks and mobile providers may also require it.
rows.evidence_quote: Your employer needs it for payroll. Your bank requires the Meldebescheinigung before opening an account.

rows.fact_text: Health insurance is legally mandatory for all residents in Germany. Employees with gross income below EUR 69,300/year (2025 threshold) are automatically enrolled in statutory health insurance (GKV); higher earners and self-employed may choose private health insurance (PKV).
rows.evidence_quote: Health insurance is legally mandatory and proof is required for most registrations. Employees earning below the income threshold (EUR 69,300/year in 2025) are automatically enrolled in GKV.

rows.fact_text: GKV contribution is approximately 14.6% of gross salary plus an average 1.7% supplementary rate, split equally between employer and employee.
rows.evidence_quote: Fees: Approx. 14.6% of gross salary + avg. 1.7% supplementary, split equally between employer and employee.

rows.fact_text: Employees must register with a statutory health insurer (GKV) before or immediately upon starting work. Apply online or by phone to any statutory insurer such as Techniker Krankenkasse (TK), Barmer, AOK, or DAK.
rows.evidence_quote: You must register with a health insurer before or immediately upon starting work. Apply online or by phone to any statutory insurer. Popular options: Techniker Krankenkasse (tk.de), Barmer, AOK, DAK.

rows.fact_text: Documents required for GKV enrolment: valid passport or ID, Meldebescheinigung, employment contract or proof of self-employment/student enrolment, and previous health insurance certificate (if transferring).
rows.evidence_quote: Valid passport or ID card, Meldebescheinigung, Employment contract or proof of self-employment / student enrollment, Previous health insurance certificate (if transferring from another insurer)

rows.fact_text: GKV membership confirmation is issued within a few days; the health insurance card (Krankenversichertenkarte) is mailed within 1–2 weeks.
rows.evidence_quote: Membership confirmation within days. Health card (Krankenversichertenkarte) mailed within 1-2 weeks.

rows.fact_text: The social security number (Sozialversicherungsnummer) is automatically issued by the Deutsche Rentenversicherung when an employee enrolls with a statutory health insurer (GKV), who forwards the registration data.
rows.evidence_quote: Once you sign up with a statutory insurer, your data gets forwarded to the Deutsche Rentenversicherung (Germany's federal pension authority)

rows.fact_text: The German social security number (Sozialversicherungsnummer) is 12 digits long; once issued it stays the same for life.
rows.evidence_quote: German social security numbers are 12 digits long and always have the same format: 00 000000 A 000. Once issued, the number stays the same for

rows.fact_text: Obtaining a social security number (Sozialversicherungsnummer) is free of charge.
rows.evidence_quote: The social security number is issued by the German public pension office 'Deutsche Rentenversicherung', also known as 'DRV'.

rows.fact_text: The social security number and card (Sozialversicherungsausweis) are sent by post to the registered address; delivery typically takes 2–4 weeks after GKV enrolment.
rows.evidence_quote: When you were first registered, the Deutsche Rentenversicherung sent you a letter containing your Sozialversicherungsausweis (social security card).

rows.fact_text: Applicant must hold a university degree in a related field (natural science or humanities), or have 10+ years practical experience in a related field.
rows.evidence_quote: Engineer/Specialist in humanities/International services (Examples: scientific engineers, IT engineers, foreign language teachers, interpreters, copywriters, designers, etc.)

rows.fact_text: A Certificate of Eligibility (COE) issued by a regional immigration authority is required before applying for the visa at a Japanese embassy or consulate abroad.
rows.evidence_quote: A Certificate of Eligibility (COE) is a document that verifies the activity in which the foreigner wishes to engage while in Japan. The advantage of this document is that it reduces the time required to obtain a visa and complete immigration procedures when work or long-term stay (more than 90days) are the purposes of the trip.

rows.fact_text: Obtaining a COE takes 1 to 3 months. After receiving the COE, the applicant must enter Japan within 3 months of the designated day on the COE.
rows.evidence_quote: Obtaining a COE takes 1 to 3 months. You MUST enter Japan within 3 months of the designated day on your Certificate of Eligibility (COE), regardless of any time limits noted on the actual visa you receive.

rows.fact_text: Visa application documents include: valid passport, one visa application form, one photograph, and original or copy of COE.
rows.evidence_quote: Visa Application Form Signed by the applicant... Original Valid Passport with at least 1.5 blank pages left... Original One 2"x 2" Photo... Original & 1 Copy Certificate of Eligibility (hardcopy)

rows.fact_text: Applicant must have a signed employment contract with a Japanese employer and the work must be related to their academic or professional background.
rows.evidence_quote: Engineer/Specialist in humanities/International services (Examples: scientific engineers, IT engineers, foreign language teachers, interpreters, copywriters, designers, etc.)

rows.fact_text: Applicant must have been continuously employed at an overseas affiliated office of the same company for at least one year immediately prior to the transfer to Japan.
rows.evidence_quote: Intra-company transferee (Examples: people transferred to the Japanese branch (head office of the same company, etc.)

rows.fact_text: Required documents: passport, visa application form, one photograph, and a Certificate of Eligibility (COE). Chinese nationals must additionally submit a copy of the Chinese Family Register.
rows.evidence_quote: Necessary documents: Passport, One visa application form... Certificate of Eligibility (Note) - the original or one copy... Chinese nationals must also submit the following documents: Copy of the Chinese Family Register.

rows.fact_text: Intra-company transferees working for stock exchange-listed companies or highly trusted companies may apply for a visa without a COE, but must submit extensive verification documents.
rows.evidence_quote: intra-company transferees may get the visa issued relatively quickly even without this certificate if they are working for a stock exchange-listed company in Japan or a highly trusted company, for example a company that is well known internationally.

rows.fact_text: Permitted period of stay for Intra-Company Transferee visa is 5 years, 3 years, 1 year, or 3 months.
rows.evidence_quote: Period of stay: 5 years, 3 years, 1 year or 3 months

rows.fact_text: As of October 16, 2025, the minimum capital requirement for the Business Manager visa was raised from JPY 5 million to JPY 30 million.
rows.evidence_quote: Under the new rules, the minimum capital requirement will be raised to 30 million yen (six times the previous amount).

rows.fact_text: From October 16, 2025, Business Manager visa applicants must employ at least one full-time employee who is a Japanese national, permanent resident, spouse of Japanese national, spouse/child of permanent resident, or long-term resident.
rows.evidence_quote: Mandatory employment of at least one full-time employee who is a Japanese national, a permanent resident, spouse of Japanese national, spouse/child of permanent resident or long-term resident.

rows.fact_text: From October 16, 2025, either the Business Manager visa applicant or one of their full-time employees must possess Japanese language proficiency at CEFR B2 / JLPT N2 level or higher.
rows.evidence_quote: Either the applicant or one of the full-time employees must possess a sufficient level of Japanese language; CEFR B2 level or higher. JLPT (Japanese Language Proficiency Test) N2 or higher. BJT Business Japanese Proficiency Test 400 points or higher.

rows.fact_text: From October 16, 2025, Business Manager visa applicants must hold a master's degree or higher in business or a related field, or have at least three years of management experience.
rows.evidence_quote: Master's degree or higher in business or related field, or at least three years of management experience.

rows.fact_text: Business Manager visa applicants must have a physical business office in Japan. Virtual offices or nominal addresses are not accepted.
rows.evidence_quote: Business Premises – Applicants are required to have physical business premises suitable for the scale of their operations. Virtual offices or nominal addresses will not be accepted.

rows.fact_text: Applicants must score at least 70 points under the Highly Skilled Professional points-based evaluation system to qualify for HSP visa status.
rows.evidence_quote: Highly skilled professional visa. Period of stay: 5 years. Necessary documents: Passport... Certificate of Eligibility (Note2)... When applying for a visa as a Highly Skilled Professional, the submission of a COE is required.

rows.fact_text: HSP visa holders with 70 points may apply for permanent residency after 3 years; those with 80 points may apply after 1 year.
rows.evidence_quote: Highly skilled professional visa. Period of stay: 5 years.

rows.fact_text: Under the J-Skip (Special Highly Skilled Professional) track, applicants in research or engineering roles must hold a master's degree or higher AND earn at least JPY 20 million per year, OR have 10+ years practical experience AND earn at least JPY 20 million per year. Business management J-Skip requires 5+ years management experience and JPY 40 million annual income.
rows.evidence_quote: Applicants must have at least 10 years of practical experience in the relevant field and an annual income of 20 million yen or more.

rows.fact_text: HSP visa application requires: passport, visa application form, one photograph, and COE. COE submission is mandatory for Highly Skilled Professional visa applications.
rows.evidence_quote: When applying for a visa as a Highly Skilled Professional, the submission of a COE is required. Certificates of Eligibility are also issued for the family members of Highly Skilled Professionals upon application.

rows.fact_text: SSW applicants must be over 18 years old and in good health, and must possess the necessary occupational skills and Japanese language ability to work without particular training.
rows.evidence_quote: Those who can work in Japan as a SSW must be over 18 years old in a good health, have the necessary occupational skills to work immediately without receiving any particular training.

rows.fact_text: SSW Type 1 applicants must pass a Japanese language proficiency test at JLPT N4 level or higher, or the Japan Foundation Test for Basic Japanese (JFT-Basic) at A2 level.
rows.evidence_quote: In order to obtain a 'Specified Skilled Worker（ⅰ）' status of residence, it is necessary to pass the 'Japan Foundation Test for Basic Japanese (JFT-Basic)' or acquire the N4 certificate for the 'Japanese Language Proficiency Test (JLPT)'.

rows.fact_text: SSW Type 1 applicants must pass skill evaluation exams for the specific industry field they will work in. Those who have completed Technical Intern Training (ii) in the same field are exempt from exams.
rows.evidence_quote: In order to obtain a 'Specified Skilled Worker' status of residence, it is necessary to pass skill exams for each specified industry field, conducted within and outside Japan. (those who have satisfactory completed Technical Intern Training (ii) are exempt)

rows.fact_text: SSW Type 1 allows a maximum cumulative stay of 5 years in Japan. Family members (spouse and children) are generally not permitted to accompany under Type 1.
rows.evidence_quote: SSW（ⅰ）：Up to 5 years in total... Accompanied by family members: SSW（ⅰ）：basically not permitted

rows.fact_text: SSW Type 2 has no requirement to confirm Japanese language proficiency through tests, and allows family members (spouse and children) to accompany if requirements are met. There is no limit on the period of stay for Type 2 on a renewable basis.
rows.evidence_quote: SSW（ⅱ）：No stay limit on a renewable basis... SSW（ⅱ）：No requirement to confirm through tests,etc.... SSW（ⅱ）：Possible if fulfill the requirement(Spouse,Children）

rows.fact_text: SSW visas cover 16 designated industry fields including Nursing Care, Building Cleaning Management, Manufacturing, Construction, Shipbuilding, Automobile Repair, Aviation, Accommodation, Agriculture, Fishery, Food Manufacturing, Food Service, Forestry, Wood Industry, Automobile Transportation, and Railway.
rows.evidence_quote: The specific work you can do as a SSW in Japan is as follows, listed for each of the 16 industrial fields. Note that only SSW (i) is available in the 'Nursing Care','Automobile Transportation Business','Railway','Forestry' and 'Wood Industry' field.

rows.fact_text: Applicant must be the legally married spouse or biological child of a Japanese national. Marriage must be legally recognized in Japan.
rows.evidence_quote: Specified visa: Spouse or child of Japanese national (Examples: spouse of a Japanese national, biological child of a Japanese national)

rows.fact_text: Required documents include: passport, visa application form, photograph, and COE. Chinese nationals must also submit a copy of the Chinese Family Register and Temporary Residence Permit.
rows.evidence_quote: Necessary documents: Passport, One visa application form... Certificate of Eligibility (Note) - the original or one copy... Chinese nationals must also submit the following documents: Copy of the Chinese Family Register, Temporary Residence Permit or Residence Certificate.

rows.fact_text: A Japanese Family Registry (Koseki Tohon) from the Japanese spouse, certifying the fact of marriage, is required as part of the COE application.
rows.evidence_quote: Japanese Family Registry (Koseki Tohon) certifying the fact of your marriage

rows.fact_text: Permitted period of stay for Spouse or Child of Japanese National visa: 5 years, 3 years, 1 year, or 6 months.
rows.evidence_quote: Period of stay: 5 years, 3 years, 1 year or 6 months

rows.fact_text: Student visa applicants must have received an acceptance letter from a recognized Japanese educational institution (university, college, language school, or vocational school).
rows.evidence_quote: Student (Examples: college students, pre-college students, etc.)

rows.fact_text: Student visa applicants must demonstrate financial ability to cover tuition and living expenses. Bank statements showing at least JPY 1,200,000 or more (from applicant or financial sponsor) are commonly required.
rows.evidence_quote: Financial sponsor's (the person wishing to study in Japan or their guarantor) savings balance certificate, income certificate covering the...

rows.fact_text: For student visas, the Japanese school submits the COE application on behalf of the student. After COE issuance, the student applies for the visa at the nearest Japanese embassy or consulate.
rows.evidence_quote: Accept the offer, submit your financial supporter's documents and pay the enrollment fee. iCLA submits your COE Application to the Immigration Department.

rows.fact_text: Digital Nomad visa applicants must earn a minimum annual income of JPY 10 million (approximately USD 67,000) from their foreign employer or clients.
rows.evidence_quote: Required annual income: Annual income of an applicant must be at least 10 million yen at the time of application.

rows.fact_text: Digital Nomad visa applicants must hold private medical/travel insurance covering death, injury, and illness with a minimum of JPY 10 million coverage for medical treatment.
rows.evidence_quote: Applicant must hold a private medical travel insurance which covers death, injury, illness during their stay. As for the amount of compensation for medical treatment for injury and illness, it must be 10 million yen or more.

rows.fact_text: The Digital Nomad visa allows a maximum stay of 6 months with no extension granted. After the maximum period of stay, the applicant must wait at least 6 months before reapplying.
rows.evidence_quote: Period of stay: Six months (No extension will be granted.) After exceeding the maximum period of stay(six months) with this status of residence, an applicant must wait for six months to reapply for the same status.

rows.fact_text: Under the Digital Nomad visa, it is not permitted to work based on an employment contract with a Japanese public or private organization. Work must be for a foreign organization.
rows.evidence_quote: Under this status of residence, it is not permitted to work based on an employment contract, etc. with a Japanese public or private organization.

rows.fact_text: Digital Nomad visa holders are not issued a Residence Card (Zairyu Card).
rows.evidence_quote: Residence card will not be issued.

rows.fact_text: Applicants must be nationals of countries/regions under visa exemption arrangements (Temporary Visitor) with Japan AND subject to Japan's Tax Conventions.
rows.evidence_quote: Applicant must be nationals or citizens of countries/regions as shown in this chart (PDF), which are under the scope of the visa exemption arrangements (Temporary Visitor) and also subjected to Japan's Tax Conventions.

rows.fact_text: Digital Nomad visa documents include: visa application form with photo, passport, COE (if obtained) OR documents explaining planned activities, income proof (tax certificate, income certificate, employment contract, or client contract clearly stating contract period and amount), and insurance proof.
rows.evidence_quote: Documents proving that the applicant's annual income is JPY 10 million or more. (Note) Tax payment certificate, income certificate, employment contract, contract with a business partner (which clearly states the contract period and the contract amount.)

rows.fact_text: The COE application is made by a sponsor in Japan (employer, school, or relative) at the nearest regional immigration authority to the sponsor's place of residence — not by the applicant abroad.
rows.evidence_quote: The application for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) is made by your sponsor in Japan at the nearest regional immigration authority to his/her place of residence. Employers or schools as well as relatives could become your sponsors.

rows.fact_text: COE processing typically takes 1 to 3 months. After receiving the COE, the applicant must enter Japan within 3 months of the date specified on the COE.
rows.evidence_quote: Obtaining a COE takes 1 to 3 months. You MUST enter Japan within 3 months of the designated day on your Certificate of Eligibility (COE), regardless of any time limits noted on the actual visa you receive.

rows.fact_text: As of March 17, 2023, it is possible to receive a COE by email (digital COE). Applicants may apply for landing by presenting a printed copy of the digital COE.
rows.evidence_quote: From March 17, 2023, it will be possible to receive a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) by email and to apply for landing by presenting the...

rows.fact_text: COE process: (1) Sponsor submits COE application to regional immigration bureau with required documents; (2) Immigration bureau reviews and issues COE (1-3 months); (3) Sponsor sends COE to applicant abroad; (4) Applicant applies for visa at Japanese embassy with COE; (5) Applicant enters Japan and receives status of residence at port of entry.
rows.evidence_quote: Once the Certificate of Eligibility (COE) reaches you by way of your sponsor in Japan, you are ready to apply for a visa at the Japanese Embassy. The Embassy highly recommends obtaining a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) before applying for visa.

rows.fact_text: Mid to long-term residents newly arriving in Japan must visit their local municipal office with their Residence Card (Zairyu Card) to register their place of residence within 14 days of establishing a place of residence.
rows.evidence_quote: Mid to long-term residents must visit the counter in charge at the municipal office where they live with their residence card... to file notification of place of residence within 14 days of establishing a place of residence.

rows.fact_text: A Residence Card is issued to foreign nationals residing legally in Japan for the mid to long-term (generally those staying more than 3 months), except for those granted Temporary Visitor status, Diplomat or Official status, or special permanent residents.
rows.evidence_quote: A residence card is issued to foreign nationals residing legally in Japan for the mid to long-term who have resident status under the Immigration Control Act ('mid to long-term residents') when they are granted a residence-related permit.

rows.fact_text: The Residence Card contains: name, date of birth, sex, nationality/region, place of residence, status of residence, period of stay, card number and validity dates, and working restrictions.
rows.evidence_quote: The following information is included on a residence card: (1) Name, date of birth, sex, and nationality or region (2) Place of residence... (3) Status of residence, period of stay, and date of expiration of period of stay... (6) Working restrictions

rows.fact_text: Mid to long-term residents who change their address must notify their new municipal office with their Residence Card within 14 days of moving. Name, date of birth, gender, or nationality changes must be notified to the Regional Immigration Bureau within 14 days.
rows.evidence_quote: Mid to long-term residents who have changed their place of residence must visit the counter in charge at their new municipal office with their residence card to file notification of their place of residence within 14 days of moving to the new residence.

rows.fact_text: For non-permanent residents aged 16 or older, the Residence Card is valid until the expiration date of their period of stay. For permanent residents aged 16 or older, the card is valid for 7 years from the date of issue.
rows.evidence_quote: Residence card validity: 16 or older: Permanent residents, Highly Skilled Foreign Professional (ii): 7 years from date of issue. Non-permanent residents: Expiration date of period of stay.

rows.fact_text: Foreign residents who complete address registration at their local city or ward office are automatically assigned a My Number. A My Number notification letter is sent to the registered address via registered mail within 2-3 weeks.
rows.evidence_quote: My Number notification letter will be sent to your registered address via registered mail in 2-3 weeks. You can verify your number in the notification letter.

rows.fact_text: Any foreign national residing in Japan who is registered as a resident (has a Resident Record / Juminhyo) is eligible to receive a My Number. This includes mid to long-term residents with a Residence Card.
rows.evidence_quote: Foreign residents who have completed resident registration at a city or ward office and have a resident record can apply for a My Number Card.

rows.fact_text: After receiving the My Number notification letter, residents can apply for the physical My Number Card (Kojin Bango Card) online, by mail, or in person at the municipal office. Processing takes approximately 3-4 weeks.
rows.evidence_quote: Your My Number is issued to you once you register at your local city office the first... usually takes 3 to 4 weeks on average.

rows.fact_text: All foreign residents in Japan holding a visa valid for 3 months or longer must enroll in either employer-sponsored health insurance (Shakai Hoken) or National Health Insurance (Kokumin Kenko Hoken / NHI). Enrollment is mandatory regardless of nationality.
rows.evidence_quote: Everyone with a Japan residence card must enroll in health insurance. Your employer handles enrollment.

rows.fact_text: Employer-based Shakai Hoken (social health insurance) enrollment is mandatory for employees who work 20 hours or more per week at a covered business. Both employer and employee split the premium contributions.
rows.evidence_quote: Your employer is legally required to enroll you in Shakai Hoken if you meet all of the following: You work 20 hours or more per week.

rows.fact_text: Kokumin Kenko Hoken (National Health Insurance) is managed by local municipalities and is required for self-employed persons, students, freelancers, and those not eligible for employer-based Shakai Hoken. Registration is done at the city/ward office.
rows.evidence_quote: Kokumin Kenko Hoken (国民健康保険, National Health Insurance) is run by local municipal offices and designed for self-employed persons, students...

rows.fact_text: Enrollment in the public pension system is mandatory for all residents of Japan between the ages of 20 and 59, including foreign nationals, regardless of nationality.
rows.evidence_quote: National Pension: cover all residents of Japan between age 20 and 59. Employees' Pension Insurance: cover workers of company and public sector.

rows.fact_text: Japan's public pension system has a two-tier structure: (1) Kokumin Nenkin (National Pension) — covers all residents aged 20-59, flat monthly contribution; (2) Kosei Nenkin (Employees' Pension Insurance) — covers salaried company and public sector workers, in addition to Kokumin Nenkin.
rows.evidence_quote: Public pension system consists of a two-tier structure as follows; National Pension: cover all residents of Japan between age 20 and 59. Employees' Pension Insurance: cover workers of company and public sector.

rows.fact_text: A minimum period of 10 years of pension contributions, exemptions, or deferments is ordinarily required to receive pension benefits in Japan.
rows.evidence_quote: A minimum period of 10 years of contributions, exemptions or deferments is ordinarily required to receive benefits.

rows.fact_text: Startup visa applicants must be supported by a Japanese municipality that has an approved startup support program. The applicant must submit a business plan and receive approval from the municipality.
rows.evidence_quote: Start-up (Entrepreneur supported by municipalities in Japan and the spouse or children of the entrepreneur.)

rows.fact_text: The Startup visa is initially granted for 6 months (Designated Activities status) to allow time for preparatory business activities. Some municipalities allow extensions up to a maximum of 2 years total.
rows.evidence_quote: Startup Visa holders can stay in Japan for six months to meet such requirements and prepare for launching their new business. In some municipalities, a further...

rows.fact_text: Startup visa process: (1) Submit preparatory activity plan to an approved municipality; (2) Municipality approves and endorses application; (3) Apply for Designated Activities visa (6 months) to regional immigration bureau; (4) Regional immigration bureau grants Designated Activities residence status; (5) After completing preparations, transition to Business Manager status.
rows.evidence_quote: Foreign nationals who plan to establish a business can take advantage of this one year period to conduct preparatory activities for starting a business after...

rows.fact_text: Non-EU nationals require a Nulla Osta (work authorisation) issued under Italy's annual Decreto Flussi quota system. For 2024, the quota for non-seasonal workers was 61,250, with 165,000 total admissions planned for 2025.
rows.evidence_quote: In 2024, there are 61,250 quotas reserved for recruiting non-seasonal workers and 680 quotas reserved for registering self-employed workers.

rows.fact_text: 25,000 of the 2024 quotas are reserved for non-seasonal employees who are citizens of countries with migration cooperation agreements with Italy, including Albania, Algeria, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Morocco, Philippines, Senegal, Sri Lanka, Tunisia, Ukraine and others.
rows.evidence_quote: 25,000 quotas are reserved for non-seasonal employees who are citizens of countries with migration cooperation agreements or arrangements.

rows.fact_text: The Decreto Flussi process requires: (1) Italian employer submits Nulla Osta request to the Sportello Unico per l'Immigrazione (SUI) during click-day window; (2) worker applies for work visa at Italian consulate abroad; (3) worker arrives and applies for Permesso di Soggiorno within 8 working days.
rows.evidence_quote: employee work — For those with an employment contract. Requires nulla osta from the Prefecture via Decreto Flussi. validity: up to 2 years.

rows.fact_text: For all labour sectors other than family/socio-medical care, the employer's income (if a natural person) or turnover (if an entity) cannot be less than €30,000 per year.
rows.evidence_quote: For all other labour sectors, the employer's income (in the case of a natural person/individual enterprise) or turnover (in the case of entities and companies), cannot be less than €30,000.00 per year.

rows.fact_text: The EU Blue Card (Carta Blu UE) for highly skilled non-EU nationals is fully exempt from the Decreto Flussi annual quota system. Applications are accepted year-round with no caps or waiting lists.
rows.evidence_quote: The EU Blue Card is fully exempt from the Decreto Flussi annual quota system — no caps, no waiting lists, no 'click day' windows. Applications are accepted year-round.

rows.fact_text: For the EU Blue Card in Italy, the minimum gross salary threshold is approximately €33,500/year for 2024 (general track, 1.5x national average). In shortage sectors such as ICT and healthcare, the threshold is approximately 1.2x the national average (~€28,000/year).
rows.evidence_quote: For Italy, the minimum salary threshold in 2024 is set at: 33.500 EUR.

rows.fact_text: EU Blue Card applicants must hold a university degree of at least 3 years, OR a post-secondary professional qualification lasting at least 3 years, OR at least 5 years of professional experience in a highly qualified field (per Legislative Decree 152/2023 implementing EU Directive 2021/1883).
rows.evidence_quote: A university degree of at least 3 years (any recognized discipline) ... At least 5 years of professional experience equivalent to a higher education qualification — particularly relevant for IT specialists, engineers, and senior managers

rows.fact_text: The EU Blue Card requires a valid employment contract for a highly qualified position lasting at least 12 months. The employer must apply for a Nulla Osta through the Sportello Unico per l'Immigrazione portal.
rows.evidence_quote: have a valid work contract or binding job offer for highly qualified employment with a duration of at least 6 months

rows.fact_text: The Nulla Osta for EU Blue Card is legally capped at 30 days for highly skilled workers. In practice, total timeline from first application to final permit is 3 to 6 months.
rows.evidence_quote: The Nulla Osta is legally capped at 30 days for highly skilled workers.

rows.fact_text: After 12 months of legal residency in Italy with an EU Blue Card (reduced from 18 months under previous rules), the holder can transfer to another EU member state under simplified conditions.
rows.evidence_quote: after residing legally in an EU Country for 12 months (before was 18 months) with an EU Blue Card, a non-EU citizen can enter Italy

rows.fact_text: For an ICT permit, the non-EU employee must have been employed by the same company or corporate group for at least 12 months (managers and specialists) or at least 3 months (trainees) before the transfer to Italy.
rows.evidence_quote: The period of validity of the ICT permit is of at least one year or the duration of the transfer may be extended to a maximum of 3 years for managers and specialists

rows.fact_text: ICT permits may be issued for a maximum of 3 years for managers and specialists, and a maximum of 1 year for trainees. ICT permits are exempt from the Decreto Flussi annual quota system.
rows.evidence_quote: This permit applies to managers, specialists, and trainees employed by a non-EU company for at least three months before being transferred to an affiliated

rows.fact_text: ICT permits cover three categories of transferees: managers (senior staff with decision-making authority), specialists (staff with specialised knowledge of company products/services or processes), and trainees (recent graduates undergoing training).
rows.evidence_quote: This permit applies to managers, specialists, and trainees employed by a non-EU company for at least three months before being transferred to an affiliated

rows.fact_text: The Italia Startup Visa (ISV) is available to non-EU nationals who wish to establish an innovative startup in Italy as defined under Art. 25, comma 2 of Decree Law 179/2012. Applicants must obtain a Nulla Osta from the Comitato Tecnico 'Italia Startup Visa'.
rows.evidence_quote: This visa can be requested by foreigners wishing to establish in Italy an innovative start-up Company according to Art. 25, comma 2 of DL 179/2012.

rows.fact_text: Italia Startup Visa applicants must demonstrate financial availability of not less than €50,000 dedicated to the innovative startup project, plus proof of income from their country of residence above the minimum level for exemption from healthcare contribution participation (€8,400).
rows.evidence_quote: Documentation proving financial availability dedicated to the Innovative Start-up which must be not less than Euro 50,000

rows.fact_text: The Italia Startup Visa process has 4 steps: (1) Submit business idea and documents to the Comitato Tecnico ISV at the Ministry of Economic Development; (2) receive Nulla Osta if approved; (3) apply for national self-employment visa at Italian consulate; (4) apply for Permesso di Soggiorno within 8 days of arrival.
rows.evidence_quote: application process — How to get the startup Visa in 4 quick steps

rows.fact_text: Italy's Digital Nomad / Remote Worker Visa is intended for non-EU citizens who intend to work remotely while living in Italy. It covers two sub-categories: 'digital nomads' (freelancers, consultants, independent specialists) and 'remote workers' (employees of a company who can work fully remotely). Only highly specialized workers qualifying under Art. 27-quater of Legislative Decree 286/1998 are eligible.
rows.evidence_quote: The digital nomad / remote worker visa is intended for individuals who are not EU citizens and who intend to work remotely while living in Italy.

rows.fact_text: Digital Nomad Visa applicants must demonstrate proof of legal income of at least three times the minimum necessary to pay healthcare taxes in Italy. As of 2024, the minimum legal income is no less than €24,789 per year (or equivalent in USD).
rows.evidence_quote: Proof of legal income of at least three times the minimum necessary to pay healthcare taxes in Italy. At the time of this writing in 2024, the minimum legal income is no less than 24,789 euros (or the equivalent in USD) per year.

rows.fact_text: The Digital Nomad Visa requires qualifying professions that need post-secondary degrees or at least three years' professional training or experience. Eligible professions can be demonstrated by: (1) bachelor's/master's/doctorate degree; (2) three or more years' professional experience in the same field; or (3) recognition by a professional body.
rows.evidence_quote: The visa is only available to highly specialized workers whose careers require or exceed the requirements listed in article 27-quater of the Legislative Decree n. 286 of 25 July 1998, including careers that require post-secondary degrees or at least three years' professional training or experience.

rows.fact_text: Digital Nomad Visa applicants must provide a lease, rental contract, or deed for property in Italy in the applicant's name, covering the entire duration of the visa. Third-party hospitality offers or hotel stays are not acceptable.
rows.evidence_quote: Lease, rental contract, or deed for property in Italy. The lease, rental contract, or deed must be in the applicant's name and must cover the entire duration of the visa. A third party's offer of hospitality or a hotel stay is unacceptable.

rows.fact_text: Digital Nomad Visa applicants must provide proof of travel medical insurance covering medical expenses, hospitalization and repatriation, with coverage of not less than €30,000 (or $50,000).
rows.evidence_quote: Letter or certificate of travel medical insurance showing coverage for medical expenses, hospitalization costs and repatriation for medical reasons, for the days you are outside the United States. Insurance coverage must not be less than 30,000 Euro (or $50,000).

rows.fact_text: Remote workers (as distinct from freelance digital nomads) applying for the Digital Nomad Visa must additionally provide: (1) employment contract showing a salary equal to or exceeding the applicable Italian national collective bargaining agreement minimum and not below the ISTAT median annual salary; (2) letter from employer confirming no convictions in the past five years for facilitation of illegal immigration or related labour offences.
rows.evidence_quote: Employment contract showing a salary that equals or exceeds that required by the collective contracts negotiated by the relevant Italian national union, and that in any case cannot be below the median annual salary as calculated by ISTAT

rows.fact_text: Under Decree Law 145/2024, non-EU sponsors must demonstrate at least two continuous years of legal residence in Italy before sponsoring a family member for reunification. Exceptions apply for minor children under a certain age.
rows.evidence_quote: Under the rule, non-EU sponsors must demonstrate at least two years of continuous lawful residence in Italy at the date the nulla osta application is submitted.

rows.fact_text: Required documents for family reunification include: duly completed visa application form, passport-size photo (not older than 6 months), valid passport, Nulla Osta al ricongiungimento (from the Italian sponsor), civil registry documents (marriage certificate or birth certificate), and proof of sponsor's income and housing.
rows.evidence_quote: Required documents: Duly filled application form; Passport-size photo no older than 6 months, full front and with white background; Valid passport or other

rows.fact_text: Eligible family members for Italian reunification include: spouse (not legally separated), minor children (including of the spouse), and dependent adult children who cannot support themselves due to health conditions. Parents over 65 may qualify if no other children can support them.
rows.evidence_quote: They must show the following documents: copies of passport and tax declaration or declaration of income; a criminal record; a certified identification

rows.fact_text: Non-EU students wishing to study at an Italian university for more than 90 days require a long-stay national study visa (Type D). Applicants must have pre-enrollment confirmed by the Italian higher education institution.
rows.evidence_quote: Pre-Enrollment Documentation: summary of the pre-enrollment application validated by the Italian higher education institution

rows.fact_text: Study visa applicants must demonstrate financial means of support in Italy of no less than €10,179.85 per year. For short-stay study programs, approximately $50 per day is required.
rows.evidence_quote: Proof of financial means of support in Italy of no less than EUR 10,179.85 per year.

rows.fact_text: For Italian-taught university degree programs, applicants must demonstrate Italian language proficiency at B2 level or higher (CEFR). For programs taught in other languages, B2 proficiency in that language is required.
rows.evidence_quote: Certification of Italian language proficiency at B2 level or higher.

rows.fact_text: For study abroad program participants, the Italian university's letter must confirm a minimum of 20 hours per week of attendance.
rows.evidence_quote: confirming the enrolment of the student, program dates, duration, weekly hours of attendance (minimum 20 hours a week)

rows.fact_text: For Bachelor's degree programs, applicants must provide the original secondary school diploma with either a CIMEA Statement of Comparability/Verification or a Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore) issued by the relevant Italian Consulate/Embassy.
rows.evidence_quote: For Bachelor's degree programs: original secondary school diploma with one of the following: – CIMEA Statement of Comparability/Verification; or – Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore)

rows.fact_text: The Elective Residence Visa (Visto per Residenza Elettiva) is intended for persons who wish to reside permanently in Italy and can demonstrate high self-sustaining income from passive sources (pensions, property rental, investments). Holders are NOT allowed to work in Italy.
rows.evidence_quote: the elective residency visa is intended for persons who wish to reside permanently in Italy and who can demonstrate high self-sustaining income and financial assets and can demonstrate a steady and adequate income (not deriving from subordinate work)

rows.fact_text: For the Elective Residence Visa, income must be 'substantial and stable' from secure sources such as pensions, property rental income, or business activities. Income from employment is ineligible. Applicants must provide recent letters from banks, financial institutions, and last 2 years of income tax returns.
rows.evidence_quote: Documented and detailed guarantee of substantial and stable private income originating from stable and secure sources such as pensions, property rental income, business activities. Income from work is ineligible for the purposes of this visa.

rows.fact_text: Processing time for the Elective Residence Visa may be up to 90 days. Rush processing is not possible.
rows.evidence_quote: The processing time for this visa may be up to 90 (ninety days). Therefore it is advisable to submit a visa request ninety days prior the expected departure date. Rush processing is not possible.

rows.fact_text: Elective Residence Visa applicants must provide a signed rental agreement per Italian rental regulations, or a deed of ownership of a livable apartment/house in Italy registered with the Agenzia delle Entrate. Hotel bookings and third-party hospitality cannot be accepted.
rows.evidence_quote: a signed rental agreement according to Italian rental regulations OR a deed of ownership of a livable apartment or house in Italy and proof of registration with the 'Agenzia delle Entrate' (the Italian Tax Agency). Multiple bookings for houses/hotels and third party offer of hospitality cannot be accepted

rows.fact_text: All non-EU citizens intending to stay in Italy for a period longer than 90 days must apply for a Permesso di Soggiorno (residence permit). EU, EEA (Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein) and Swiss citizens are exempt. The permit is issued by the Questura competent for the applicant's territory of residence.
rows.evidence_quote: All non-EU citizens intending to stay in Italy for a period longer than 90 days are required to apply for a residence permit.

rows.fact_text: The Permesso di Soggiorno application process: (1) Go to an authorized post office (Sportello Amico) and collect the Kit Giallo (yellow kit) for free; (2) Complete and submit the kit at the same counter; (3) Receive an SMS or registered letter with the date of appointment at the Questura for fingerprinting (fotosegnalamento). The postal receipt serves as a temporary document while waiting.
rows.evidence_quote: 1. Presentation of the Kit Postale — Go to an authorized post office ('Amico' counter) and collect the Kit Postale Free.

rows.fact_text: The total cost for a Permesso di Soggiorno in 2026 is approximately €116 to €176: postal payment slip (€30.46) + residence permit fee (€40 for permits up to 1 year, €50 for 1–2 years, €100 for EU long-term) + kit postale shipping (€30.00) + revenue stamp (€16.00, exempt for minors).
rows.evidence_quote: Cost: from €100 (€30.46 postal orders + €70.46 + stamp duty)

rows.fact_text: Permesso di Soggiorno processing times vary significantly by city: Bologna 30–60 days, Turin 45–90 days, Florence 45–90 days, Milan 60–120 days, Naples 60–150 days, Rome 90–180 days.
rows.evidence_quote: Bologna 30 - 60 days ... Milan 60 - 120 days ... Rome 90 - 180 days — The most crowded Questura in Italy

rows.fact_text: After regular entry into Italy with a valid entry visa, every non-EU citizen who wishes to stay for more than 90 days must apply for a residence permit within 8 working days from arrival.
rows.evidence_quote: within 8 working days from his arrival.

rows.fact_text: Required documents for the Permesso di Soggiorno application include: valid passport or equivalent with entry visa, 4 colour passport photos (45x35mm, white background), Codice Fiscale (tax ID), documentation relating to the reason for stay (employment contract, university enrollment, etc.), certificate of housing suitability or rental agreement, and €16.00 revenue stamp.
rows.evidence_quote: Valid passport or equivalent document with entry visa — 4 color passport photos (45x35 mm, white background) — Tax ID code — Documentation relating to the reason for your stay

rows.fact_text: Non-EU citizens who have resided legally in Italy for at least 5 continuous years may apply for an EU long-term residence permit (Permesso di Soggiorno CE per Soggiornanti di Lungo Periodo). Requirements include an A2 Italian language test and adequate income.
rows.evidence_quote: EU long term — For those who have resided in Italy for at least 5 years. Requires an A2 Italian language test and adequate income. Duration: unlimited.

rows.fact_text: Non-EU citizens can obtain the Codice Fiscale (Italian Tax Identification Number) either at the Sportello Unico per l'Immigrazione (for those applying for work or family reunification permits) or at any Police headquarters (Questura) when requesting or renewing a Permesso di Soggiorno, or at the offices of the Italian Revenue Agency (Agenzia delle Entrate) in person.
rows.evidence_quote: Non EU citizens can obtain the tax identification number either at the Single desk for immigration 'Sportelli Unici per l'immigrazione' or by any Police headquarters 'Questure'.

rows.fact_text: Non-EU citizens applying for a Codice Fiscale must submit at least one of the following: a valid passport with visa (if required); any other document accepted by Italian authorities; a certificate of identity issued by Italian diplomatic/consular authorities; a valid Permesso di Soggiorno; or an ID card issued by the Italian municipality of residence. Non-EU citizens must also prove the right to stay in Italy.
rows.evidence_quote: Citizens from non-EU Countries must submit at least one of the following documents: a valid passport with visa (if required), or any other document accepted by the Italian authorities ... Non-EU citizens must also prove that they have the right to stay, even temporarily, in Italy.

rows.fact_text: Non-resident individuals who need to obtain a Codice Fiscale before arriving in Italy can apply for it at the Italian consular authorities in their country of residence.
rows.evidence_quote: Non-resident individuals who need to obtain the tax identification number can apply for it to the Italian consular authorities in the Country of residence.

rows.fact_text: EU and non-EU foreign citizens applying for their first Italian Codice Fiscale must book an in-person appointment at an Agenzia delle Entrate office. The applicant must appear in person for identity verification.
rows.evidence_quote: EU and non-EU foreign citizens applying for their first Italian tax identification number (codice fiscale) must book an in-person appointment at the office. The applicant must go to the counter in person so that their identity can be verified.

rows.fact_text: Social security obligations for hiring non-EU workers in Italy are identical to those for Italian and EU employees. Employers must register with the Italian Social Security Administration (INPS) and pay contributions.
rows.evidence_quote: Social-security obligations for hiring non-EU workers in Italy are identical to those for Italian and EU employees.

rows.fact_text: Italian employers who hire foreign workers (EU or non-EU) must register with INPS and pay contributions in Italy for all work carried out on Italian territory, in accordance with Italian social security law.
rows.evidence_quote: If the worker works for an employer (Italian or foreign) operating in Italy, social security contributions must be paid in Italy in accordance with

rows.fact_text: Foreign nationals legally residing in Italy with a valid Permesso di Soggiorno (for work, family reunification, or asylum reasons) are entitled to mandatory and free registration with Italy's Servizio Sanitario Nazionale (SSN) at the local ASL (Azienda Sanitaria Locale).
rows.evidence_quote: Foreign nationals who wish to apply for a health-card must first register with the National Health Service (SSN). contact the competent ASL.

rows.fact_text: Non-EU students on a study visa can access the SSN through voluntary enrollment for a fee of approximately €700/year. This is not mandatory but gives access to the same public healthcare as residents. Alternatively, students may purchase private health insurance.
rows.evidence_quote: Non-EU students on a study visa have two options: Option A: SSN Enrollment (€700/year) The ASL accepts this as temporary proof of legal

rows.fact_text: After registering with the SSN at the local ASL, foreign nationals receive a tessera sanitaria (health card) — a personal health card issued by Agenzia delle Entrate that enables access to Italy's public healthcare system.
rows.evidence_quote: Foreign nationals who wish to apply for a health-card must first register with the National Health Service (SSN). contact the competent ASL.

rows.fact_text: All non-EU foreign nationals with a valid permit allowing stay are required to register their residency at the Anagrafe (Vital Records/Registry Office) of the municipality (Comune) where they intend to establish residence. This registration is required for access to public services.
rows.evidence_quote: All non-EU citizens with a permit allowing stay are required to register with the municipality where they plan to establish their residence.

rows.fact_text: Non-EU citizens must register with the Anagrafe (registry office) at the Comune (city hall) of the municipality where they reside. The Codice Fiscale must be obtained from the Agenzia delle Entrate before applying for residency. Registration triggers access to local services including healthcare, school enrollment and public transport discounts.
rows.evidence_quote: You must register with the Anagrafe if: You move to Italy and intend to stay more than 90 days. You are non EU/EEA citizen staying in Italy for more than 90 days

rows.fact_text: Upon arrival in Italy, non-EU nationals must comply with the obligation to declare their presence within 8 working days by applying for the Permesso di Soggiorno. The Questura issues a declaration of stay. Failure to comply may result in administrative expulsion.
rows.evidence_quote: Il cittadino straniero entro 8 (otto) giorni lavorativi, dall'ingresso in Italia, deve adempiere agli obblighi derivanti dalle norme relative al soggiorno sul territorio dello Stato, avanzando istanza di richiesta di Permesso di Soggiorno

rows.fact_text: Holders of an Italian Elective Residence visa must register with the local Police Department (Questura) within 8 days of arrival in Italy to obtain the Permesso di Soggiorno ('Declaration of Stay'), which is the only legal document that legitimises their stay.
rows.evidence_quote: Within 8 days upon arrival in Italy, you must register with the local Police Department (Questura) to obtain the 'Declaration of Stay' (Permesso di Soggiorno), which is the only legal document that legitimizes your stay in the country.

rows.fact_text: Employer applies for an Employment Entry Permit through MOHRE (for mainland) or the relevant Free Zone authority. The employee enters the UAE on this entry permit and must complete all residence visa steps within 60 days of entry.
rows.evidence_quote: The foreigner is granted a work entry visa ... which permits the holder to remain in the country for (60) sixty days starting from the date of entry or until the necessary processes for granting residence have been completed.

rows.fact_text: After entering the UAE on the entry permit, the employee must undergo a mandatory medical fitness test at an approved government health centre. The test screens for HIV, tuberculosis (TB), and — for certain worker categories including food handlers, domestic workers, nursery staff, and salon workers — also Hepatitis B and syphilis. A 'Fit' result is required to proceed with visa stamping.
rows.evidence_quote: In order to be able to obtain a work/residence permit, foreign nationals need to be free of all forms of communicable diseases such as HIV and TB.

rows.fact_text: Concurrent with or immediately after the medical test, the employee applies for an Emirates ID card through ICP (Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security). This requires biometric data collection (fingerprints and photograph) at an ICP service centre. Processing takes 7–14 business days for the standard service.
rows.evidence_quote: Individuals who have completed 15 years of age are required to complete the fingerprint and signature procedures through the Authority's service centers.

rows.fact_text: Once the medical test returns 'Fit' and Emirates ID is processed, the Residence Visa is stamped in the employee's passport by GDRFA (Dubai) or the relevant emirate authority. This must be completed within 60 days of entry on the Entry Permit. The standard employment visa is currently valid for 2–3 years (extended to 3 years as of April 2025) and is renewable.
rows.evidence_quote: Standard employment visa extended from 2 to 3 years. Reduces renewal frequency. Eases financial burden on employers.

rows.fact_text: MOHRE issues a digital Labour Card (Work Permit) as the final step, confirming that employment is officially authorised.
