rows.label_en: Tax card (skattekort) in employer's system BEFORE first paycheck
rows.fact_text: Obtain a Norwegian electronic tax card (skattekort) from Skatteetaten after receiving the D-number. The tax card is made available to the employer electronically, and the employer is obliged to retrieve it and keep the information updated before every payroll run (skattebetalingsloven § 5-1). NON-OBVIOUS DEADLINE: the tax card must be in the employer's system BEFORE the first paycheck — without access to the tax-card information the employer must withhold 50 % of gross salary (§ 5-5). Over-withheld tax can be recovered, but the process delays the employee's net pay.
rows.evidence_quote: (2) Arbeidsgiver plikter å innhente skattekort før inntektsårets begynnelse for de personlige skattyterne arbeidsgiver plikter å foreta forskuddstrekk for, og sørge for at skattekortopplysningene er oppdaterte før hver lønnskjøring, slik at forskuddstrekket blir foretatt etter siste beregnede skattekort.

NON-OBVIOUS DEADLINE: it must be in the employer's system BEFORE the first paycheck — without it, 50% of gross must be withheld. Over-withholding is recoverable but delays the employee's net pay.

rows.label_en: EEA registration with the Norwegian police within 3 months
rows.fact_text: An EEA national who stays in Norway under a residence right (e.g. as a worker) for more than three months must register; the registration deadline is three months from the date of entry (utlendingsloven § 117). For registration as a worker, the police may require a valid identity card or passport and confirmation of employment from the employer. Failure to register is punishable with a fine (§ 108 first paragraph). Book the appointment early — the registration is done at the police or a Service Centre for Foreign Workers, and a registration certificate is issued immediately once the documentation is presented.
rows.evidence_quote: En EØS-borger som oppholder seg i riket etter §§ 112 eller 113 i mer enn tre måneder, skal registrere seg. Fristen for registrering er tre måneder fra innreisedatoen. Når EØS-borgeren framlegger dokumentasjon som nevnt i annet og tredje ledd, utstedes straks et registreringsbevis.
rows.source_version: Utlendingsloven (LOV-2008-05-15-35) § 117 første ledd, lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret LOV-2026-06-19-50 fra 01.07.2026
rows.authored_by: cursor-cloud-agent (automated source re-verification 2026-08-16) — pending human authoring review
rows.official_guidance: EEA nationals don't need to do anything special to stay in Norway.
rows.actual_reality: An EEA national staying over 3 months must register with the police — the deadline is 3 months from entry. The police may require ID/passport and employer confirmation of employment; failure to register is punishable with a fine. The certificate is issued immediately once documents are presented.
rows.action_required: Book the police / Service Centre for Foreign Workers appointment early and register within 3 months of entry; bring passport and employer confirmation of employment.

rows.label_en: EEA registration certificate (registreringsbevis) — issued once, not renewed
rows.fact_text: The EEA registration certificate (registreringsbevis) is issued immediately and free of charge once the required documentation is presented, and it is not renewed — it is a one-time registration confirming the police have registered the EEA national (utlendingsforskriften § 19-22). Keep it: it is commonly requested as proof of legal residence when opening a bank account, registering in the National Registry, and completing other administrative steps. Registration and issue happen at the police in the district of residence or at a Service Centre for Foreign Workers, and can be done electronically.
rows.evidence_quote: Registeringsbevis med opplysninger om den registrertes navn, adresse og dato for registrering utstedes straks og vederlagsfritt. Registreringsbeviset skal ikke fornyes. (§ 19-22 annet ledd)
rows.source_version: Utlendingsforskriften (FOR-2009-10-15-1286) § 19-22, lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret FOR-2026-06-19-1132 / FOR-2026-06-25-1375
rows.authored_by: cursor-cloud-agent (automated source re-verification 2026-08-16) — pending human authoring review
rows.official_guidance: The registration certificate is a minor formality you can lose track of.
rows.actual_reality: The EEA registration certificate (registreringsbevis) is issued immediately and free, is never renewed (one-time), and is commonly requested as proof of legal residence when opening a bank account, registering in the National Registry and completing other steps.
rows.action_required: Keep the registration certificate safe after issue — it is reused as residence proof for banking and folkeregister steps.

rows.label_en: Open a Norwegian (NOK) bank account to receive salary
rows.fact_text: Open a NOK bank account at a Norwegian bank to receive salary. Norwegian banks are legally required to collect the customer's name, fødselsnummer or D-number, and address before opening an account for a natural person, and to confirm identity against valid identification (hvitvaskingsloven § 12) — so the D-number gates this step for a new arrival, and the police registration certificate is commonly requested as supporting documentation. Bank onboarding for non-residents takes time in practice, so start the account opening early: it sits on the critical path to the employee actually being paid.
rows.evidence_quote: Når kunden er en fysisk person, skal følgende opplysninger innhentes om kunden: a. navn b. fødselsnummer, D-nummer eller, dersom kunden ikke har slikt nummer, annen entydig identitetskode ... c. adresse. (§ 12 første ledd)
rows.source_version: Hvitvaskingsloven (LOV-2018-06-01-23) § 12, lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret LOV-2026-02-06-2
rows.authored_by: cursor-cloud-agent (automated source re-verification 2026-08-16) — pending human authoring review

Non-resident onboarding is slow in practice and sits on the critical path to actually being paid.
rows.action_required: Start the bank-account opening early with the D-number and registration certificate ready — it is a common bottleneck to the first salary landing.

rows.label_en: National Registry (Folkeregisteret) registration — report in person within 3 months and 8 days
rows.fact_text: An EEA national covered by Directive 2004/38/EC who moves to Norway to settle in a Norwegian municipality must, within three months and eight days after arrival, report the move in person at the tax office and present a passport or equivalent identification (folkeregisterforskriften § 6-5-4 second paragraph). Registration as resident is what moves the employee from the temporary D-number onto a Norwegian national identity number (fødselsnummer), since the D-number is reserved for persons who do not meet the conditions for one (§ 2-2-3). Bring the passport, the police registration certificate, the employment contract and proof of a Norwegian address to the appointment.
rows.evidence_quote: Person som omfattes av direktiv 2004/38/EF om EØS-borgere og deres familiemedlemmers rett til å bevege og oppholde seg fritt på medlemsstatenes område og som flytter til Norge for å bosette seg i norsk kommune, skal innen tre måneder og åtte dager etter ankomsten personlig melde dette på skattekontoret og vise frem pass eller tilsvarende legitimasjon.
rows.source_version: Folkeregisterforskriften (FOR-2017-07-14-1201) § 6-5-4 annet ledd, lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret FOR-2025-12-17-2639
rows.authored_by: cursor-cloud-agent (automated source re-verification 2026-08-16) — pending human authoring review

rows.actual_reality: An EEA national settling in a municipality must report the move IN PERSON at the tax office within 3 months and 8 days of arrival, with passport. This is what moves the employee from the temporary D-number onto a permanent national identity number (fødselsnummer).
rows.action_required: Book the in-person tax-office appointment within ~3 months of arrival; bring passport, police registration certificate, employment contract and proof of a Norwegian address.

rows.label_en: Which country's social security applies (EEA Reg. 883/2004) — CONSULT PROFESSIONAL
rows.fact_text: For an employee moving from France, social-security liability (French vs Norwegian national insurance / folketrygden) is coordinated under Regulation (EC) 883/2004, which applies as Norwegian statute law through folketrygdloven § 1-3 a, together with implementing Regulation (EC) 987/2009. Whether the employee stays in the French scheme (e.g. via an A1 posting certificate) or joins Norwegian folketrygden depends on the structure of the move. This is a CONSULT-PROFESSIONAL determination: a regulated advisor must decide the applicable scheme and obtain any certificate. Getting it wrong creates double contributions or a coverage gap.
rows.evidence_quote: EØS-avtalen vedlegg VI nr. 1 (forordning (EF) nr. 883/2004 om koordinering av trygdeordninger ...) (trygdeforordningen) gjelder som lov med de tilpasningene som følger av vedlegg VI, protokoll 1 og avtalen for øvrig. (§ 1-3 a første ledd)

rows.label_en: Valid identity card or passport held throughout the stay
rows.guidance: SCOPE NOTE ON THE CITED PARAGRAPH: § 117 annet ledd does not itself impose a general obligation to carry identification. It presupposes a valid identity card or passport (“i tillegg til gyldig identitetskort eller pass”) and governs the ADDITIONAL documents the police may require for registration; the “kan” applies to those additional documents. The provision that conditions the right of residence itself on holding valid identification is § 111 første ledd: “En EØS-borger som har gyldig identitetskort eller pass, har oppholdsrett i inntil tre måneder, forutsatt at vedkommende ikke blir en urimelig byrde for offentlige velferdsordninger.” Counsel should attest the two provisions together.
rows.fact_text: An EEA national must hold a valid national identity card or passport to have a right of residence in Norway, and must present that document when registering with the police, which may additionally require the employer's confirmation of employment.

applies_to.timing: Valid before departure and for the whole of the stay in Norway.

rows.label_en: Compulsory folketrygden membership for a person resident in Norway
rows.guidance: Residence is defined in § 2-1 annet ledd: a stay of at least 12 months, counted from the date of entry. § 2-1 tredje ledd adds that lawful residence is a condition of membership. The employment route is § 2-2 første ledd: “En person som ikke er medlem i trygden etter § 2-1, er likevel pliktig medlem i trygden dersom han eller hun er arbeidstaker (§ 1-8) i Norge eller på den norske delen av kontinentalsokkelen i forbindelse med leting etter eller utvinning av olje, gass eller andre naturressurser.” NAV states the same rule in English: “Membership as a resident: If you live in Norway, you are as a general rule a member of the National Insurance Scheme.” (https://www.nav.no/en/home/rules-and-regulations/membership-of-the-national-insurance-scheme). PROFESSIONAL REVIEW REQUIRED: § 2-1 a provides that chapter 2 is set aside so far as necessary for the EEA social-security coordination rules, so a valid A1 certificate can displace Norwegian membership for a posted worker.
rows.fact_text: A person resident in Norway is a compulsory member of the Norwegian National Insurance Scheme (folketrygden), and an EEA national who works in Norway without being resident is a compulsory member on the basis of that employment.

applies_to.timing: From the date of entry when the stay is intended to last at least 12 months.

rows.evidence_quote: Personer som er bosatt i Norge, er pliktige medlemmer i folketrygden.
rows.source_version: Folketrygdloven (LOV-1997-02-28-19) § 2-1 første ledd, lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret LOV-2026-06-19-45 fra 01.07.2026, LOV-2026-06-23-65
rows.authored_by: otto/claude-2026-08-16

rows.actual_reality: Membership is not optional: a person resident in Norway is a compulsory member of the National Insurance Scheme (folketrygden), and an EEA national who works in Norway without being resident is a compulsory member on the basis of that employment.
rows.action_required: Assume compulsory folketrygden membership unless an A1 / 883-2004 coordination outcome says otherwise — factor employer and employee contributions into the cost model.

rows.label_en: Portable document A1 obtained before departure from France
rows.guidance: WHICH FRENCH INSTITUTION: the request is filed with Urssaf Service mobilité internationale for the régime général, or with the Mutualité Sociale Agricole (MSA) for the agricultural scheme. CLEISS states the formality and its timing — “Avant le départ de votre salarié à l'étranger, vous devez informer l'organisme compétent et obtenir une attestation de la législation applicable à votre salarié, le document portable A1 (art. 15 du règlement (CE) 987/2009) :” — and adds that the request must state the reasons for the assignment, the place where it will be carried out and, where applicable, the name and address of the undertaking the employee will temporarily work for (https://www.cleiss.fr/employeurs/empl_france_envoie_ue_ue.html). Norway is in scope of that page, which names “en Norvège” among the destination states. POSTING PERIOD: “Le détachement est de 24 mois (art. 12, §1 du règlement (CE) 883/2004).” A posting that exceeds that period from the outset, or an extension beyond it, is possible only by exceptional agreement under Article 16 of Regulation (EC) 883/2004, applied for through Urssaf (or the MSA); the cited sources state no maximum duration for such an agreement, so the only period that may be relied on is the one Urssaf or the MSA actually authorises. PROFESSIONAL REVIEW REQUIRED: whether French cover is maintained at all depends on the posting conditions CLEISS lists for the employer and the employee (a subordination link maintained with the French employer, the employer normally carrying on significant activity in France, the employee not replacing another posted worker on the same assignment, and — where the employee was recruited in order to be posted — having been subject to French legislation for at least one month before being hired). A valid A1 also bears on Norwegian social security: it can displace compulsory folketrygden membership for a posted worker — see the folketrygden membership step.
rows.fact_text: Before a French employer sends an employee to work temporarily in Norway, it must inform the competent French institution (Urssaf Service mobilité internationale, or the MSA for the agricultural scheme) and obtain portable document A1 certifying that French social security legislation remains applicable to that employee.

applies_to.timing: Before the employee departs France for the Norwegian assignment.
